categories.title: Airway, Oxygen And Emergency Care
categories.body: Equipment used to maintain airway, support breathing and manage urgent clinical situations.

items.name: Air Ring
items.imageAlt: Air Ring medical instrument reference image
items.use: Air Ring is used in airway care, respiratory support, oxygen delivery or secretion management.
items.preparation: Check size, patency, cleanliness, required accessories and patient identity; explain the procedure and prepare infection prevention supplies.
items.safety: Monitor breathing, oxygenation and patient response; avoid prolonged or forceful use and escalate respiratory distress promptly.
examPoints: Identify Air Ring by its correct name and category.
State the main use in one clear sentence.
Mention preparation before use, including cleanliness or sterility where relevant.
Give one patient-safety or infection-prevention point.

items.name: Laryngoscope
items.imageAlt: Laryngoscope medical instrument reference image
items.use: A laryngoscope is used to open the upper airway and visualize the larynx, epiglottis and vocal cords during endotracheal intubation, airway assessment and emergency airway management.
items.preparation: Select the correct blade and handle, check that the light works, inspect the blade for cleanliness and damage, prepare oxygen, suction, bag-valve-mask, appropriate endotracheal tubes, syringe, tape or tube holder, monitoring equipment and PPE; position the patient safely and explain the procedure when possible.
items.safety: Use under trained supervision, monitor oxygen saturation and pulse, avoid levering against the teeth or lips, limit repeated attempts, maintain cervical-spine precautions when trauma is suspected, clean or sterilize according to policy after use and document the airway intervention.
examPoints: Identify the instrument as a laryngoscope and name the main parts: handle, blade and light source.
State that it is used to visualize the vocal cords during endotracheal intubation or airway assessment.
Before use, check blade size, handle connection, battery or bulb/light function, cleanliness and availability of suction and oxygen.
Mention correct patient positioning, usually sniffing position unless cervical-spine injury is suspected.
Give safety points: avoid dental/lip trauma, monitor oxygenation, stop prolonged attempts and maintain infection prevention.
